identity_notes: The retrieved literature for 'OI_BEETROOT_POWDER' is dominated (68 of 114 records) by agricultural/plant-science and livestock/companion-animal-feed studies of sugar beet (Beta vulgaris) as a CROP or FIBER-BYPRODUCT ingredient — entirely unrelated to beetroot as a nitrate-rich human dietary supplement — plus several 1990s-era 'sugar beet fibre' human diabetes/lipid trials that concern a distinct manufactured fiber ingredient, not beetroot root powder/juice; all were excluded as off_topic, animal_or_invitro, or different_substance. The single most important applicability caveat for the genuine human beetroot-nitrate evidence base: results are highly outcome- and dose-dependent and frequently null in well-controlled trials — the largest acute running trial (n=70, PMID 32470923) and the longest RCT (24 weeks, PMID 33340674, in type 2 diabetes) both found NO significant benefit over placebo, and a dose-response trial (PMID 41704173) found different cardiovascular endpoints responded to different, non-overlapping doses (endothelial function only at 400 mg nitrate, aortic blood pressure only at 800 mg, with no effect on brachial blood pressure at any dose tested). Many 'positive' trials combined beetroot/nitrate with a supervised exercise program, another active ingredient (citrulline malate, creatine, vitamin C, whey protein, caffeine, mushroom extracts), or diet intervention common to both study arms, limiting attribution to beetroot alone; product forms also vary substantially (raw juice, cooked beet, betalain-standardized concentrate, nitrate-depleted comparator, powder, and even microgreens), which may not be interchangeable.
